name: broker
description: node-broker — throw a raw request at a local MCP server and drive the harness flow as a node graph it owns. graph_open builds plan/setgoal/critique and, once setgoal returns a spec, expands per-subgoal implement/test/gate plus a goal gate and report — all server-side, so the spec never passes through the orchestrator. graph_next says which nodes are ready and how each is routed; graph_run has the routed vendor execute one (blocking, with the prompt composed by the broker from graph state, not passed in); graph_submit records one the orchestrator did itself. Both paths meet the same worktree cross-check and the same dependency guard: a claimed changed_file the worktree does not show fails the node, and the broker may lower stage_ok but never raises it. Tools return a one-line verdict, never the payload — handoffs, acceptance, evidence and changed-file lists stay on disk, which is what keeps a long retry loop from exhausting the orchestrator context. vendor:auto falls back to self; a named vendor fails instead, so a run can prove which vendor did the work. Vendors are a registry — codex ships built in via adapters/codex-exec-adapter.mjs, projects add more in .claude/broker-vendors.json against the same adapter CLI contract. Sibling to the harness plugin: harness owns the six-stage reasoning contract, broker owns the graph, routing, execution, adjudication, and the ledger at <cwd>/.harness-run/broker/, which a PreToolUse gate reads to treat a running node as engagement. Zero runtime dependencies: newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio.
